summary: Third independent exact-head reproduction confirms worker-status vocabulary drift is broader than CLAIMING. Swarm Control run 31471294857 at control SHA ebe1aad771c0d34457dbf05637e459f70e99cf33 passed all 23 core and 17 hardening tests, then failed live-state validation because sol-20260811-p6v4n8 used status DONE. That worker subsequently self-reconciled the same completed lifecycle state to canonical STOPPED. This demonstrates workers are inventing intuitive aliases for lifecycle states because the canonical vocabulary is not exposed in the Go protocol.
evidence: Actions run 31471294857 / validate-control-branch: 23 core tests OK and 17 hardening tests OK, followed by invalid worker status on sol-20260811-p6v4n8.json.
At exact failing control SHA ebe1aad771c0d34457dbf05637e459f70e99cf33, sol-20260811-p6v4n8.json contains status DONE.
The current live record for the same worker now contains canonical status STOPPED with otherwise equivalent completion semantics.
Earlier independent exact-head failures already captured CLAIMING as another intuitive but non-canonical alias.

metadata.implication: A durable repair should address the worker-facing lifecycle vocabulary and semantic alias failure mode, not just rewrite individual malformed records. Any compatibility handling must preserve STOPPED fail-closed ownership semantics rather than treating DONE as an active state.
